holidays.name: National Cake Day
holidays.description: Today is a day with a built-in excuse to eat dessert. Bakers, frosting fans and office break-room regulars slice into a favorite cake, from towering layer cakes to humble cupcakes. Sharing is encouraged. Seconds are traditional.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance with no single known founder. It has become a popular fixture on the food-holiday calendar, and it often lands in the middle of Thanksgiving dessert season.
holidays.funFact: Early cakes were more like sweetened bread. Modern fluffy cakes only became common after chemical leaveners like baking powder arrived in the 19th century.

holidays.name: Good Grief Day
holidays.description: This is a day for saying "good grief" and meaning it. It nods to life's small disasters, like a kite eaten by a tree or a football pulled away at the last second. Shrug off the day's mishaps with a dramatic sigh and a sense of humor.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is widely linked to the cheerfully gloomy spirit of Charlie Brown and the Peanuts gang.
holidays.funFact: Charlie Brown made "good grief" one of the best-known exclamations in comics. It is a mild phrase that fits nearly any minor catastrophe.

holidays.name: Coton de Tulear Day
holidays.description: This day honors the Coton de Tulear, a small, fluffy, cotton-soft dog known for being cheerful, clownish and devoted to its people. Dog lovers celebrate with cuddles, treats and a good brushing for these living cotton balls.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance celebrating the breed, which comes from Madagascar. The breed is named after the port city of Tuléar, now called Toliara.
holidays.funFact: The Coton de Tulear is the official dog of Madagascar. Its soft, cottony coat is where the breed gets its name.
